podcast-joerogan-QOrOYUxzX3o:
Director Oliver Stone sits for episode 1511 of the Joe Rogan Experience, a long-form talk on film and power. Stone made Platoon, JFK, and Nixon, films that argue with official history. Rogan treats him as both artist and witness to the events his work covers.

Stone talks about how his films get made, what the studios resist, and why he keeps returning to presidents and wars. Rogan asks about the lines between fact and drama in his movies. The episode is a veteran director's account of using cinema to fight over the nation's memory, at full length.
podcast-tuckercarlson-Uyh62MUEC3o:
Commentator Ana Kasparian, co-host of The Young Turks, crosses over to Tucker Carlson in this episode. The fiery left-wing host and the conservative Carlson find surprising common ground. Their talk covers the Epstein cover-up, an Israeli strike on a Gaza church, and a great shift in American politics.

Kasparian gives her case that both parties serve the same donor class. She and Carlson agree on Epstein's protection and on disgust with party machines. They part on plenty, but the shared ground is the story here. Political and open-minded viewers get strange bedfellows arguing in a fiery hour.
